derivation: Recorded baselines: logs/idle-memory-before-oMVPIO and logs/idle-memory-after-9nrfCt (17 Oct 2026, owner's Linux x64 host, 16 logical CPUs, loaded, swap in use) and logs/idle-memory-baseline-Lv23NI (19 Oct 2026, this branch before the process-sampling and traversal changes, 4 CPUs, Xvfb, no swap).
Time to Explorer and startup peak family PSS: the largest of the three baselines plus about 25%, rounded up (cold 10,503 ms / 1,947.0 MiB; warm 8,645 ms / 1,851.0 MiB).

Idle private growth (USS + swap) per role between the idle marks: Lv23NI at most 2.7 MiB per role; the always-local host was flat (112.9 -> 112.5 MiB) in the 18 Oct telemetry probe after the OV-1005 transport guard. The 9nrfCt +155 MiB host growth came from the hosted-call loop that guard removed and is not a valid baseline. Limits allow scheduler and GC noise, not the old loop.

Idle CPU seconds per role per 10 minutes: 9nrfCt renderer 7.51, main 1.74 (process scan active), three quiet extension hosts 2.6 each; Lv23NI renderer 9.86, all four extension hosts 14.99, main 0.56. The main limit is below the 9nrfCt value, which included the 10 s whole-system scan.
Long session: process count flat (9nrfCt and Lv23NI 16 -> 16), private slope 6.7 and 6.2 MiB per iteration after the terminal release (29.8 before it), 0 killed-terminal shells and 0 pty masters.

Quick variant: 1 and 2 minute idle marks, 2 iterations. Its two-point slope and one-minute CPU window are noisy (wpzbLK: 77.8 MiB slope), so those two limits are wider. It is a smoke check, not a substitute for the full run.
